units.text: If your spouse dies, you may be eligible for survivor benefits based on their work record.
supporting_chunk_ids: Explore The Benefits You May Be Due#2_0::c0000
units.reason: The context states that if your spouse dies, you may be eligible for higher survivor benefits based on their work record.

units.text: Generally, you can receive survivor benefits as a widow/widower if you are at least age 60 (age 50 if disabled), or at any age if you are caring for their child who is under 16 or disabled.
units.reason: The contexts do not specify age requirements for survivor benefits; they only mention that you may be eligible if your spouse dies. The specific age thresholds are not present.

units.text: If you remarry before age 60 (age 50 if disabled), you cannot receive benefits as a surviving spouse while married; remarriage after that age does not disqualify you.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Survivors | If You Are The Survivor | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0012
units.reason: The context explicitly states that remarriage before age 60 (50 if disabled) disqualifies you while married, and remarriage after that age does not disqualify you.

units.text: Benefits may be reduced if you start early, and there are earnings limits if you work.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Survivors | If You Are The Survivor | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0012
units.reason: The context mentions limits on earnings for survivors and that benefits may be affected by early retirement, though the exact reduction details are not specified.

units.text: If you also qualify for your own retirement benefit, you can switch to the higher amount at full retirement age.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Survivors | If You Are The Survivor | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0012
units.reason: The context states that a widow/widower can switch to their own retirement benefit if it is higher, and can switch at full retirement age.

units.text: For exact eligibility and amounts, contact Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 or visit your local office.
